news.title: LWN.net Weekly Edition for June 11, 2026
news.abstract: Welcome to the LWN.net Weekly Edition for June 11, 2026 This edition contains the following feature content: AI agent runs amok in Fedora and elsewhere : a Fedora developer spotted suspicious contributions that seem to be from a "rogue" AI agent. Moving beyond fork() + exec() : an attempt to address process-creation shortcomings in the kernel. Splicing out vmsplice() : LLM-discovered vulnerabilities may lead to removal of splice() and vmsplice() . More coverage from the 2026 Linux Storage, Filesystem, Memory Management, and BPF Summit : BPF loop verification with scalar evolution : an algorithm used in compilers could help the BPF verifier handle more loops. An update on fanotify : what has been merged in the last year and what is pending for the filesystem-event monitoring subsystem. Eliminating long-lived credentials with trusted publishing : a look at a method to thwart supply-chain attacks with short-lived credentials. This week's edition also includes these inner pages: Brief items : Brief news items from throughout the community. Announcements : Newsletters, conferences, security updates, patches, and more. news.summary: 这是LWN.net 2026年6月11日的周刊摘要，主要内容涉及Fedora中AI代理异常贡献、fork()+exec()进程创建机制的改进讨论，以及vmsplice()系统调用相关的LLM发现的漏洞。文章重点关注内核进程管理、安全漏洞和发行版开发，与Linux内核网络子系统无直接关联。
